text: Copy before change; one root per version.

A persistent balanced tree (可持久化平衡树) keeps every version of a set or sequence. FHQ Treap (拓展篇第4章) is the easy one to make persistent: split and merge only touch nodes on a root path, so copy each node before changing it. Every operation then creates O(log n) new nodes and a new root, and old roots still describe old versions (P3835).

Treap priorities are random and never change, so a copied node keeps its priority and the expected shape is unchanged. The sequence version with lazy reversal (P5055) must also copy children when pushing a tag down, because the children may be shared with other versions.

Each line "v op x" works on version v and creates version i. Random operations on random old versions, checked against keeping a separate sorted list for every version in Python. A query creates copies too, but they are thrown away because the version keeps the old root.
Memory: every operation copies O(log n) nodes, so size the pool for (operations × about 50) nodes. Never modify a node that may belong to another version; always copy first (split does it here).
Accept worse moves with e^(−Δ/T); cool slowly.
Simulated annealing (模拟退火): a randomised search for the minimum of a messy function. Keep a current point and a temperature T. Each step moves to a random nearby point (step size proportional to T).
Accept it if it is better; if it is worse by Δ, still accept it with probability e−Δ/T. Cool T slowly (multiply by 0.99…). High T explores; low T settles.

It has no guarantee: use it for partial scores or when nothing exact is known, and run it several times from random starts within the time limit. Hill climbing is the T = 0 version (accept only improvements, shrink the step): exact when the function is convex, as in 平衡点(P1337), the weighted point minimising Σ wi·distance.

The weighted geometric median of 8 random points, checked against Weiszfeld's iteration (an exact convergent method) in Python. The final hill-climbing phase with halving steps polishes the annealing result to full precision.

Tune by experiment: starting temperature on the scale of the coordinates, cooling factor 0.99–0.999, and stop by time (clock()) rather than by a fixed count on a real judge. Always keep the best point seen, not just the current one.

Key points to memorise
1. Persistent FHQ: copy every node split/merge changes; old roots stay valid.
2. Pool size ≈ operations × 50; push-down must also copy shared children.
3. Annealing: random step ∝ T; accept worse with e^(−Δ/T); T *= 0.99x; keep the best.
4. Convex objective ⇒ plain hill climbing with shrinking steps is exact.
